edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. I, 8

source_text: Adnuntia mihi, quem dilexit anima mea, ubi pascis, ubi cubas in meridie. Non quaero alia tempora, quando vespere, quando diluculo, quando in solis pascis occubitu; illud tempus inquiro, quando florente die, quando plena luce in maiestatis tuae splendore versaris. Adnuntia mihi, quem dilexit anima mea, ubi pascis, ubi cubas in meridie. Diligenter observa, ubi meridiem legeris. Apud Ioseph meridie fratres prandium celebrant, angeli meridie Abrahae suscipiuntur hospitio, et cetera istiusmodi. Quaere et invenies scripturam divinam non frustra et fortuitu unumquemque usurpare sermonem. Quis putas est dignus e nobis, ut ad meridiem usque perveniat et videat, ubi pascat, ubi cubet sponsus in meridie? Nisi enim mihi tu adnuntiaveris, incipio errabunda iactari et, dum te quaero, in aliorum greges incurrere.
pass_a_gloss: Announce to-me whom soul of-me loved, where you-pasture, where you-lie at-noon. I-do-not seek other times (evening/dawn/sunset); I-seek when day flowering, full light, in majesty's brightness. Observe carefully where you-read noon: Joseph's brothers lunch at noon; angels hosted by Abraham at noon; Scripture not in-vain each word. Who worthy to reach noon and see where bridegroom pastures/lies? Unless you announce, I begin wandering tossed and while seeking you run upon others' flocks.
notes: Pass A literalist gloss ≠ Pass B literary English.
Song lemma sense-checked against Baehrens; Lawson ACW not used for wording.
pass_b_english: Tell me, you whom my soul has loved, [[where you pasture, where you lie down at noon >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:7]]. I do not ask about other times — when in the evening, when at dawn, when you pasture at the sun’s setting. I seek that time when the day is in flower, when in full light you move in the brightness of your majesty. Tell me, you whom my soul has loved, where you pasture, where you lie down at noon. Watch carefully wherever you read “noon.” In Joseph the brothers take their meal at noon; angels are received as Abraham’s guests at noon; and other such things. Search and you will find that divine Scripture does not take up each word vainly and by chance. Who among us, do you think, is worthy to reach as far as noon and see where the Bridegroom pastures, where he lies down at noon? For unless you tell me, I begin to be tossed about wandering, and while I seek you I run upon others’ flocks.
